extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism adjudication from sections 3.3.1-3.3.3 and Figs. 3-6; claims are bounded to membrane permeability/sonoporation interpretation and CD structure context.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TGH2 combined with low-intensity ultrasound increases E. coli membrane permeability compared with individual treatments, supported by conductivity and ONPG permeability assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TGH2 plus 0.3 W/cm2 ultrasound against Escherichia coli
mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact plotted numeric series are figure-embedded and were not converted into separate quantitative records; mechanism conclusion is source text plus figure-caption supported.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TEM morphology shows membrane-associated damage context under TGH2 and ultrasound, including internal solute leakage and vacuolation in E. coli cells.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TGH2 plus 0.3 W/cm2 ultrasound against Escherichia coli
mechanism_claims.limitations: TEM supports membrane-damage morphology but does not by itself quantify pore number, pore size, or a molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The authors interpret the enhanced antimicrobial effect as sonoporation-facilitated membrane permeabilization that enables TGH2 entry and bacterial killing.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: combined low-intensity ultrasound and TGH2 treatment

mechanism_claims.limitations: This remains the paper authors' integrated interpretation from membrane assays and TEM; it is not a single isolated molecular-target assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD spectroscopy indicates TGH2 has alpha-helical structure in SDS and low-intensity ultrasound causes only slight untwisting rather than destroying the secondary structure.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TGH2 peptide structure under 0.3 W/cm2 ultrasound
